Done. Here's a summary of your codebase:

**Stack**
- Backend: Node.js + Express + PostgreSQL (`pg`), running on port 3001
- Frontend: Angular (AdminLTE template), running separately

**Backend structure** (`backend/inventoryBackSystem/`)
- `server.js` / `index.js` — HTTP server + Express app setup with CORS
- `connection.js` — PostgreSQL pool via `dotenv` config
- `schema.sql` — 9 tables: `book`, `warehouses`, `status`, `categories`, `products`, `vendors`, `customers`, `stocks`, `order_details`, `delivery_details`
- `routes/` — one file per resource, maps HTTP verbs to controllers
- `controller/` — CRUD controllers with pagination + keyword search for all entities
- `services/stockupdate.js` — `saveStock` (called on order create) and `decreaseStock` (called on delivery create) to auto-update stock quantities

**Frontend structure** (`frontend/.../src/app/`)
- `services/product.service.ts` — main Angular service hitting the backend API
- `components/` — one component per entity: products, vendors, customers, orders, delivery, stocks, warehouses, categories, status
- `template/` — AdminLTE layout shell (sidebar, header, footer, wrapper)
- `model/inventory.model.ts` — TypeScript interfaces

**Notable observations**
- In `orderController.js`, `stockService.saveStock()` is called *after* `res.status(200).json(...)` — the stock update runs fire-and-forget outside the try/catch, so errors there are silently swallowed.
- Same pattern in `deliveryController.js` with `decreaseStock`.
- No authentication/authorization middleware is present on any route.
- `warehouseid` is hardcoded to `1` in `stockupdate.js` when inserting a new stock record.

Let me know what you'd like to work on.

All done. Here's a summary of what was finished:

**Backend fixes:**
- `orderController.js` & `deliveryController.js`: `findTotalSale` now uses `SUM(total_price) AS sum` — the old query returned a key named `sum(total_price)` which PostgreSQL doesn't alias, so the dashboard was always showing `undefined`.

**Frontend fixes:**
- `main-wrapper.component.ts` (Dashboard): `loadProduct`, `loadVendor`, `loadCustomer`, `loadStatus` now correctly use `.data` from the `PagedResult` response with `limit=100` so all items are available for the filter lookups. The `sum` key extraction was also corrected.
- `stocks.component.html`: Uncommented the "Create New" button and the Action column (edit + delete icons) — the TS had full CRUD but the UI had it all commented out.
- `delivery.component.html`: Added the missing pagination nav below the table (every other component had it, delivery was missing it).

Your pagination is **already fully implemented end-to-end** and working correctly. Nothing needs to be changed.

Here's exactly how it works right now:

**Backend** — every route does:
```
SELECT * FROM products ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT $1 OFFSET $2
```
with `page` and `limit` from query params (default `limit=10`). Returns `{ data, total, page, totalPages }`.

**Frontend** — every component:
- Starts at `page = 1`, fetches only 10 rows
- Has `goToPage(p)` that updates `this.page` and re-fetches
- Shows pagination nav only when `totalPages > 1`
- Search also resets to `page = 1`

So with 1 million rows, the first request only loads 10 rows. Clicking page 2 fetches the next 10. The database does the heavy lifting with `OFFSET`.

The only thing to be aware of: at very large offsets (e.g. page 100,000), `OFFSET` gets slow in PostgreSQL. If that ever becomes a problem, you'd switch to cursor-based pagination (using `WHERE id < last_id`), but for a typical inventory system that's not a concern.

Which page/component are you on? (e.g. Products, Stocks, Delivery, Orders...)

Also — the pagination nav only shows when `totalPages > 1`, which means you need more than 10 rows in the database. With very little data right now, if you have ≤10 rows the nav is intentionally hidden.

Can you tell me which page you're looking at, and roughly how many rows are in that table?

Yes — I added the pagination nav to `delivery.component.html` (it was the only one missing it). All other components already had it.

But as I said — the nav is hidden when `totalPages > 1`, meaning it only appears when you have **more than 10 rows** in that table. With little data right now, you won't see it.

To test it quickly, just add 11+ rows to any table and the pagination will appear.

Here's the SQL to insert 50 products. Run this in **pgAdmin** (Query Tool) or **psql**:

```sql
INSERT INTO products (pcode, pname, pcate, price, createdate)
SELECT
  'PRD-' || LPAD(gs::text, 3, '0'),
  (ARRAY['Laptop','Mouse','Keyboard','Monitor','Headset','Webcam','USB Hub','SSD','RAM','Printer',
         'Scanner','Router','Switch','Cable','Charger','Desk Lamp','Speaker','Microphone','Tablet','Phone'])[((gs-1) % 20) + 1]
  || ' ' || gs,
  (gs % 4) + 1,
  ROUND((RANDOM() * 990 + 10)::numeric, 2),
  NOW() - (gs || ' days')::interval
FROM generate_series(1, 50) gs;
```

This inserts 50 products with:
- Codes `PRD-001` to `PRD-050`
- Realistic product names cycling through 20 types
- Category IDs 1–4 (make sure you have at least 4 categories)
- Random prices between $10–$1000
- Staggered create dates

After running it, refresh your Products page and you'll see pagination with 5 pages of 10 each.

Default encapsulation — Angular scopes the CSS to the component, so styles on `<aside>` will work fine since it's inside the component template. All good.

Done. One file, covers everything across all pages:

**What changed globally:**
- **Page background** — soft `#f4f6fb` instead of plain white
- **"Create New" button** — red gradient matching the sidebar, with hover lift effect
- **Search input & selects** — rounded, clean border, red focus ring
- **Table header** — dark navy gradient (`#1a1a2e → #0f3460`) with white uppercase text

The problem was AdminLTE's `.table-striped thead th` or `.table thead th` was overriding the color back to dark. Added `background: transparent` on `th` so the gradient from `tr` shows through, and added more specific selectors to force `color: #ffffff`. The headings should now be clearly visible as white text on the dark navy background.

Two changes made:

1. **Update button hover** — added explicit `color: #fff !important` on `:hover`, `:focus`, `:active` so Bootstrap can't override it to dark text.

2. **Table header** — changed from dark navy to a lighter indigo-purple gradient (`#4f46e5 → #7c3aed`) which is softer on the eyes, and added `border-radius` on the first and last `th` so the header row has rounded top corners.

- **Header** — back to `#1a1a2e → #0f3460` (exact same as sidebar)
- **Update button** — collapsed all states (default, hover, focus, active, visited) into one rule with `color: #fff !important` so Bootstrap has no chance to override it to dark/white

The root cause was AdminLTE's `adminlte.css` hardcoding `color: #1f2d3d` (near-black) on `.btn-warning` and every hover/focus/active state — no amount of `!important` in `styles.css` could beat it because it loads after. Changed all those states directly to `color: #fff` in the source. The Update button will now show white text in all states.
Now the Update button will have dark `#1f2d3d` text on an amber gradient background in all states — clearly readable.

Here's what the new dashboard has:

**Row 1 — KPI Cards (4 cards):**
- Total Purchase — dark navy gradient
- Total Sales — green gradient
- Revenue — teal (positive) or red (negative) depending on value
- Products count — purple gradient

**Row 2 — Summary Mini Cards (3 cards):**
- Vendors count — amber
- Customers count — red/pink
- Recent Transactions (orders + deliveries combined) — navy

**Row 3 — Two side-by-side tables:**
- Latest Purchase Orders with product, qty, price, vendor, status badge
- Latest Deliveries with product, qty, price, customer, status badge
- Status shown as colored pill badges (red/blue/green/amber) instead of raw text
- Empty state message when no data
- "View All →" link and "+ New" button on each

Improvements made:

- **KPI cards** — deeper gradients, decorative circle overlay in top-right corner, stronger hover lift + shadow
- **Summary cards** — icon shadow, stronger hover effect
- **Table cards** — hover shadow on the whole card, "View All" link now has a pill border that glows on hover
- **Section labels** — "Overview", "Quick Stats", "Recent Activity" in small uppercase grey above each section
- **Empty state** — inbox icon + message when no data
- **Product name** bolded in table rows for quick scanning
- **Background** — slightly deeper `#f0f2f8` for more contrast against white cards

Done. Cards are now compact:

- KPI cards: `14px 16px` padding, `42px` icon, `1.15rem` value font
- Summary cards: `14px 18px` padding, `40px` icon, `1.4rem` number font

Not registered. Two options:

**Option A — Install `ng2-charts` (recommended, Angular-native)**
```bash
npm install ng2-charts chart.js
```
Gives you `<canvas baseChart>` directive — clean, typed, reactive.

**Option B — Use Chart.js from assets (no install)**
Register the existing `Chart.bundle.min.js` in `angular.json` scripts and call `new Chart()` directly in the component with `declare var Chart: any`.

Which do you prefer? Option A is cleaner but requires an install. Option B works with what you already have, zero install needed.

Done. The dashboard now has two charts between the summary cards and the tables:

- **Bar chart (8 cols)** — "Purchase vs Sales" side-by-side bars in navy and green
- **Doughnut chart (4 cols)** — "Orders vs Deliveries" with a 70% cutout, legend at bottom

Both charts are reactive — they update automatically when the API data loads.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS book (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255),
    price NUMERIC(10,2),
    dept_id INT
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS warehouses (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    wname VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS status (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    status VARCHAR(100)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS categories (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    cname VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS products (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    pcode VARCHAR(100),
    pname VARCHAR(255),
    pcate INT,
    price NUMERIC(10,2),
    createdate TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS vendors (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    address TEXT,
    cell VARCHAR(50),
    contact_person VARCHAR(255),
    company VARCHAR(255),
    email VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS customers (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    address TEXT,
    phone VARCHAR(50),
    customer_name VARCHAR(255),
    email VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS stocks (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    quantity NUMERIC(10,2),
    productid INT,
    warehouseid INT,
    updatedate TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS order_details (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    quantity NUMERIC(10,2),
    productid INT,
    unit_price NUMERIC(10,2),
    statusid INT,
    total_price NUMERIC(10,2),
    vendorid INT,
    createdate TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS delivery_details (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    quantity NUMERIC(10,2),
    productid INT,
    customerid INT,
    deliverydate DATE,
    unit_price NUMERIC(10,2),
    total_price NUMERIC(10,2),
    statusid INT,
    createdate TIMESTAMP
);

Done. Here's a summary of your codebase:

**Stack**
- Backend: Node.js + Express + PostgreSQL (`pg`), running on port 3001
- Frontend: Angular (AdminLTE template), running separately

**Backend structure** (`backend/inventoryBackSystem/`)
- `server.js` / `index.js` — HTTP server + Express app setup with CORS
- `connection.js` — PostgreSQL pool via `dotenv` config
- `schema.sql` — 9 tables: `book`, `warehouses`, `status`, `categories`, `products`, `vendors`, `customers`, `stocks`, `order_details`, `delivery_details`
- `routes/` — one file per resource, maps HTTP verbs to controllers
- `controller/` — CRUD controllers with pagination + keyword search for all entities
- `services/stockupdate.js` — `saveStock` (called on order create) and `decreaseStock` (called on delivery create) to auto-update stock quantities

**Frontend structure** (`frontend/.../src/app/`)
- `services/product.service.ts` — main Angular service hitting the backend API
- `components/` — one component per entity: products, vendors, customers, orders, delivery, stocks, warehouses, categories, status
- `template/` — AdminLTE layout shell (sidebar, header, footer, wrapper)
- `model/inventory.model.ts` — TypeScript interfaces

**Notable observations**
- In `orderController.js`, `stockService.saveStock()` is called *after* `res.status(200).json(...)` — the stock update runs fire-and-forget outside the try/catch, so errors there are silently swallowed.
- Same pattern in `deliveryController.js` with `decreaseStock`.
- No authentication/authorization middleware is present on any route.
- `warehouseid` is hardcoded to `1` in `stockupdate.js` when inserting a new stock record.

Your pagination is **already fully implemented end-to-end** and working correctly. Nothing needs to be changed.

Here's exactly how it works right now:

**Backend** — every route does:
```
SELECT * FROM products ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT $1 OFFSET $2
```
with `page` and `limit` from query params (default `limit=10`). Returns `{ data, total, page, totalPages }`.

**Frontend** — every component:
- Starts at `page = 1`, fetches only 10 rows
- Has `goToPage(p)` that updates `this.page` and re-fetches
- Shows pagination nav only when `totalPages > 1`
- Search also resets to `page = 1`

So with 1 million rows, the first request only loads 10 rows. Clicking page 2 fetches the next 10. The database does the heavy lifting with `OFFSET`.

The only thing to be aware of: at very large offsets (e.g. page 100,000), `OFFSET` gets slow in PostgreSQL. If that ever becomes a problem, you'd switch to cursor-based pagination (using `WHERE id < last_id`), but for a typical inventory system that's not a concern.

Here's the SQL to insert 50 products. Run this in **pgAdmin** (Query Tool) or **psql**:

```sql
INSERT INTO products (pcode, pname, pcate, price, createdate)
SELECT
  'PRD-' || LPAD(gs::text, 3, '0'),
  (ARRAY['Laptop','Mouse','Keyboard','Monitor','Headset','Webcam','USB Hub','SSD','RAM','Printer',
         'Scanner','Router','Switch','Cable','Charger','Desk Lamp','Speaker','Microphone','Tablet','Phone'])[((gs-1) % 20) + 1]
  || ' ' || gs,
  (gs % 4) + 1,
  ROUND((RANDOM() * 990 + 10)::numeric, 2),
  NOW() - (gs || ' days')::interval
FROM generate_series(1, 50) gs;
```

This inserts 50 products with:
- Codes `PRD-001` to `PRD-050`
- Realistic product names cycling through 20 types
- Category IDs 1–4 (make sure you have at least 4 categories)
- Random prices between $10–$1000
- Staggered create dates

After running it, refresh your Products page and you'll see pagination with 5 pages of 10 each.
